recipient: Cloudflare Technical Support through the Support dashboard for the SHIFT account
subject: My Timber Workers: multi-second response delay — request runtime trace
body:
Please investigate intermittent multi-second response latency affecting My Timber on shiftsometimber.co.uk.

Cloudflare account: 9e5386dcf455be34c582d93f8bfc79e6
Zone: shiftsometimber.co.uk (66ec3268950adcfc837b7b8b2f8356ed)

Reproducible anonymous incident:
2 November 2026, 20:59:55.720 UTC
GET https://shiftsometimber.co.uk/member/dashboard?view=app
CF-Ray: a54610c94f810c18-LHR
HTTP 200; final response headers 2,654ms; complete response 2,667ms.

The matched Core execution used 39ms CPU and 41ms wall time, while its caller recorded an 827ms Core wait. Programme used 280ms CPU / 1,114ms wall time; Support 9ms / 2,152ms; Documents 19ms / 2,220ms. Exact Worker names, versions and timestamps are attached.

A production Programme CPU profile recorded 3,761ms garbage collection out of 4,079ms sampled CPU. Reducing fixed-data artifacts from 93.61MB to 23.05MB did not meet our retained 1,755ms p95 requirement. We also reproduced an internal identity/gzip mismatch and tested a narrow correction: 12 correctness checks passed, but n20 p95 was 4,154ms against a 2,972ms simultaneous control. Neither candidate was promoted.

Please trace the missing time through Worker dispatch, cold initialisation, scheduling/garbage collection and response streaming/compression. Identify the specific application or platform cause and the corrective action supported by that trace.

Use only the supplied anonymous incident; no member records are needed. Please investigate under our existing support entitlement. Obtain our approval before any chargeable work, plan change or production change.

Shift Some Timber Ltd
